name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2025-62593 — Ray-Project Ray Code Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Ray-Project Ray. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 21 August.

items.title: Coverage Is Not Containment: A Fundamental Limit of Admission-Time Defenses Against Coordinated Poisoning of Vector Retrieval
items.dek: Coordinated poisoning of vector stores defeats admission-time RAG defenses; 10 unremarkable injected documents seize top-k retrieval in 88% of cases.
items.unproven: whether defenses at retrieval time or generation time can mitigate the attack; whether the attack succeeds across all vector databases and embedding models.

items.title: Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks by Verifying What Actually Happened
items.dek: Reworded memory forgeries evade SENTINEL defense on first attempt; stronger models (GPT-4o 98–100%) more vulnerable; PoEM uses HMAC-chained tamper-evident logs.
items.unproven: whether PoEM prevents attacks when agents can modify or exfiltrate the ledger itself; real-world agent latency and storage overhead; whether sophisticated rewording defeats PoEM's integrity assumptions.

items.title: Beyond Single-Vulnerability Evaluation: Closing the Engineering Decision Gap Between C Retrofits and Native Safety
items.dek: Layered C memory-safety retrofits incur compounding performance penalties and protection gaps compared to native Rust or Go; cross-language benchmark exposes the engineering gap.
items.unproven: whether the standardized tasks cover the full attack surface of production C codebases or deployment patterns in financial services.

items.title: Inferring 1-Minimal Trigger Configurations for Assessing Linux Kernel CVE Triggerability
items.dek: FCC framework infers minimal Linux kernel configurations that trigger CVEs, improving post-olddefconfig success from 62.5% to 96.6% on 88 CVEs.
items.unproven: Evaluated on KernelCTF and KernJC only; reproducer availability not quantified; applicability to vendor workflows outside academia unclear.

items.title: AI-Generated GitHub Copilot "Autofix" Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira
items.dek: Copilot-generated fix introduced authentication bypass in Snowflake's Jira; suggests checking AI-assisted remediation for security regressions.
items.unproven: whether this pattern is systematic across codebases or isolated to this incident; no measurement of fix-suggestion safety across large corpus

items.title: CompoSkill: Compositional Skill Chain Attacks from Individually Scanner-Passing LLM Agent Skills
items.dek: Scanner-passing LLM agent skills compose into exploitable chains; existing per-skill verification misses path-level risks.
items.unproven: Bench scale and real-world marketplace risk quantification unclear; no evidence of exploitation in deployed agent ecosystems.

items.title: Conjunctive Poisoning in AI Supply-Chain Applications
items.dek: Prompt wrappers and metadata files can conjunctively alter LLM/VLM output without touching weights; tested on 15 models; TIF-BAH defense verifies wrapper integrity and behavioral attestations.
items.unproven: whether TIF-BAH can be bypassed via supply-chain compromise of the middleware itself; whether wrapper scanning tools and SigStore adoption are operationally feasible at deployment scale.

items.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do
items.dek: Eight evaluation choices in power-system attack detection benchmarks reverse conclusions before model selection; labels, not pipeline, explain accuracy.
items.unproven: whether the identified methodological flaws propagate to defenses deployed in operational power systems; quantum models remain unproven against classical on this problem.

items.title: Pre-Model Representation Failures in GNN-Based Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
items.dek: GNN-based smart contract detectors fail due to hardcoded 47-variable whitelist, byte-identical graphs from structurally different contracts, and missing reentrancy semantics.
items.unproven: Analysis limited to GNNSCVulDetector; evasion attack effectiveness on defended systems not tested; generalization to other GNN detectors unestablished.

items.title: What to Remember, What to Reveal: Privacy-Aware Memory for Conversational Agents
items.dek: Privacy-aware memory architecture separates sanitized content from exact PII in conversational agents with selective retrieval.
items.unproven: Benchmark is task-specific; no evidence that soft isolation prevents extraction attacks or handles agent jailbreaks; user consent model is underspecified.

items.title: LLMs for Zero-Shot Threat Detection via Structured Risk Indicators
items.dek: Two-stage LLM framework generates risk indicators from security logs to detect insider threats and APTs with 11–31 point F1 gains.
items.unproven: Evaluation on two fixed benchmarks only; no cross-dataset generalization; RAG dependency on historical data completeness unexamined; live SOC integration untested.

items.title: Decorrelation Is Not Complementarity: Skill, Not Lineage, Governs Trusted-Monitor Ensembles
items.dek: Monitor skill, not decorrelation or lineage, predicts ensemble gain in trusted detection; pairwise correlation metric misleads.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to backdoored-code detection; generalization to other attack types and integration into SDLC workflows untested.

items.title: Provenance, Not Behaviour: A Serialisation Artifact in Edge-IIoTset and a Leakage-Free Benchmark for Precision-Agriculture Intrusion Detection
items.dek: Edge-IIoTset benchmark's 99% intrusion detection accuracy collapses to 95% when a serialization artifact encoding file provenance is removed.
items.unproven: whether the corrected benchmark reflects real-world IIoT deployments or generalizes beyond the curated subsets tested.

items.title: Maintaining IoT Device Identification under Concept Drift via Budget-Aware Traffic Labeling
items.dek: IoT device classifiers degrade under concept drift; uniform sampling of deployment traffic outperforms drift-detector-selected instances for capturing behavioral evolution.
items.unproven: whether findings generalize across network environments beyond enterprise and ISP settings tested; retraining costs and labeling overhead not quantified.

items.title: TwinGridShield: Consequence-Aware Runtime Authorization for LLM Grid-Agent Actions
items.dek: Runtime authorization layer validates LLM-proposed grid actions against a deterministic network twin before execution; stops 84.2% configured unsafe proposals.
items.unproven: whether DC power flow model fidelity suffices for AC grid transients and whether the attack model reflects real LLM prompt-injection vulnerability in deployed systems.

items.title: Classical Adversarial Fault-Tolerance and PCPs
items.dek: Fault-tolerance scheme enabling circuit compilation against adversarial bit corruption yields new polylogarithmic-query PCP construction.
items.unproven: feasibility of quantization roadmap; practical instantiation of PCP results

items.title: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation with Adversarial Errors
items.dek: Fault-tolerance theorem for quantum circuits tolerating adversarial corruption of almost-linear qubit fraction per timestep.
items.unproven: implementation on near-term quantum hardware; scaling behavior beyond theoretical bounds

items.title: Hundred-hertz quantum circuit iteration rate in a reusable neutral-atom array
items.dek: Neutral-atom processor achieves 101 Hz quantum circuit iteration rate via non-destructive readout and atom reuse.
items.unproven: scaling to larger qubit counts; sustained performance over extended runs; practical error correction integration

items.title: DSPrompt: Dynamic Soft Prompt Defense Against M-RAG Corruption
items.dek: Soft-prompt layer insertions defend multimodal RAG retrievers against adversarial embedding attacks without pipeline modification.
items.unproven: Evaluation is against online attacks from paper's own attacker; no evaluation against held-out attack families or real-world poisoning; inference cost trade-off unclear.

items.title: DCI: Dependency Confidence Index for Assessing Open-Source Dependency Trustworthiness
items.dek: Dependency Confidence Index combines nine factors into trust score for PyPI packages; moderate agreement with OpenSSF Scorecard.
items.unproven: Validation limited to 92 popular PyPI packages; unclear which trust factors should shift selection decisions in practice.

items.title: Recovering Process Variables from Industrial Network Traffic via Search-Based Optimization
items.dek: Protocol reverse engineering via search optimization recovers process variables from industrial network traffic without historian access.
items.unproven: Tested on unspecified industrial deployments; no comparison to manual reverse engineering or field validation of recovered semantics.

items.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
items.dek: DeepSeek Harness agent resists indirect prompt injection with 16–25.5% attack success rates across 14,560 controlled tests.
items.unproven: Evaluation on isolated fixtures with recorded side effects, not live external integrations; results specific to this agent harness.

items.title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline
items.dek: Just-in-time pipeline detects and remediates AI-generated Python vulnerabilities using CodeQL, Bandit, and LLM validator; 9–54% finding reduction.
items.unproven: Evaluation on 26 synthetic prompts only; no measurement of false positives, false negatives, or remediation quality in real SDLC.

items.title: SkillWatermark: An Embedded Skill Watermark of Progressive Privacy Inference via Benign Prompts
items.dek: Watermarked skill descriptions in LLM agent prompts produce observable traffic patterns that encode private information across conversation turns.
items.unproven: whether traffic pattern encoding is distinguishable under normal network noise and rate limiting; whether this covert channel survives prompt-injection defenses or agent output filtering.

noise.title: Incident with Github.com
noise.dek: GitHub experienced an incident; status page notification with no technical detail disclosed.
noise.unproven: incident scope, root cause, and whether reader's infrastructure was affected remain unknown

noise.title: Anthropic's War on open source AI
